intro.title: Cookie-Based Auth Flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple login system that uses cookie-based authentication. You'll learn how to securely handle user credentials by storing authentication tokens in HTTP-only cookies instead of local storage or session storage. The core programming concept involves making HTTP requests with credentials included and managing authentication state in a React application. You'll work with React components, TypeScript interfaces, and HTTP request handling to create a complete login/logout flow. By the end, you'll understand why cookie-based auth is more secure for certain applications and how to implement it properly.
intro.usecase: Cookie-based authentication is essential for secure web applications where user sessions need to persist across browser sessions. You'll implement this pattern in admin dashboards like Shopify's merchant portal, where merchants stay logged in while managing products and orders. This approach is also used in banking applications like Chase Online, where sensitive financial data requires persistent, secure sessions without constant re-authentication. As a developer, you'll apply this when building any application requiring user accounts with protected routes and seamless session management.
